advances: A finite menu of equal actual critical caps with prescribed positive rates at a core-fiber maximum; padding puts the local ratio below target but gives a deeper site elsewhere.

proof:
The endpoint hull gives the exact middle Minkowski average. At $\lambda=0$, $A_0$ is the triangle with vertices $(0,0),(1,-1),(1,1)$. The half-difference body $(A_0-A_0)/2$ has vertices $(0,\pm1),(\pm1/2,\pm1/2)$ and area $3/2$. Adding the vertical segment of length $2\lambda$ increases its area by $2\lambda$ because its horizontal width is one. Thus the respective areas are $1+2\lambda,3/2+2\lambda,1+2\lambda$. Full mixed reflection about $Y$ preserves the core, so every containing closed halfspace has at least half its mass. A nonvertical through-cap boundary has zero mixed area, and each such cap has exactly half the mass, $Q$. The complementary pair with margins $\pm(x-1)$ covers the whole ambient space at mass $Q$, proving global maximality. For $H_t$ the cuts are at $x=t,1,2-t$. The endpoint sections are reflected copies, of equal length $2(t+\lambda)$, and the own section is centered at $c$ by symmetry. Therefore their summed section centroid in all base and continuous coordinates equals $Y$, and its own trace is proper since $c$ is interior to the middle fiber.

The two extreme integer layers $r=0,1$ in the padded hull retain their own hulls without mixing. The core layer thus keeps its three fibers and the other layer is the product of $[0,24]$ and the padding rectangle. There are no other integer layers. Both layers contain their full relative dimensions and their hull is full dimensional. The padded masses give $9Q<M$ for $0<\lambda\le1/4$, and every fiber area is at most $2<M/9$. The added term $-100r$ strictly excludes the padding from $H_t$ because $x\le4$, $z\ge0$ and $t-1<0$ there. The half-core lower bound at $Y$ persists, with the extended cap attaining it. The opposite core cap, extended by subtracting $100r$ from its reversed core margin, also strictly excludes padding since $z\le24$ and $x\ge3$. These caps cover the entire core anchor plane, proving fiberwise maximality there. Extend the opposite margins $\pm(x-1)$ and $\pm y$ in the same way to obtain the stated spanning menu. Central symmetry of the padding layer about its integer center gives its lower bound $25/2$, strictly larger than $Q$.

For $\epsilon>0$, set $C(\epsilon)=\exp[-M_\lambda^{-1}\int\log(x+\epsilon)\,d\mu_\lambda]$, with $M_\lambda$ the mass of the chosen family. Then $\log(\epsilon C(\epsilon))$ strictly increases because its derivative is $1/\epsilon-\mathbb E[(x+\epsilon)^{-1}]>0$ under the normalized measure. Its limit is zero as $\epsilon\to\infty$. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$ the log expectation remains bounded and $\log\epsilon$ tends to $-\infty$. For the bound, the only fiber meeting $x=0$ is $A_\lambda$, whose $x$-density is $2(x+\lambda)$ on $[0,1]$. The integral against $|\log x|+\log 2$ is uniformly bounded for $\lambda\le1/4$ and $0<\epsilon\le1$. All other fibers have $x\ge1/2$ and $x\le4$. Thus the prescribed minimum uniquely defines $\epsilon_\lambda$, and for small $\lambda$ it has $\epsilon_\lambda<1$, since the value at $\epsilon=1$ is bounded below. The resulting $C_\lambda$ is bounded above and away from zero. The relation $\epsilon_\lambda=C_\lambda^{-1}e^{-T/\lambda}$ now gives $0<t_{\lambda,s}<1$ for each fixed $0<s<T$ and small $\lambda$.

On $A_\lambda$ the inverse measure integrated in $y$ is $2(x+\lambda)\,dx/(x+\epsilon_\lambda)$. At rate $R>0$, the substitution $x=C_\lambda^{-1}e^{-R/\lambda}-\epsilon_\lambda$ yields the density $2(x+\lambda)/\lambda$ in $R$ up to the endpoint $T$. On each interval $a\le R\le T$ with $a>0$, this density tends uniformly to $2$, and every point of the section satisfies $|y|\le x+\lambda\to0$ uniformly there. No rate lies above $T$, and the substitution shows that $T$ itself has no atom. This proves the stated convergence against continuous tests with compact support at positive rates, also after imposing $x\ge t_{\lambda,s}$, which is exactly $R\le s$. Other fibers, bounded away from $x=0$, have no contribution at positive rates. The proper section at rate $s$ has weighted log mass $2(t_{\lambda,s}+\lambda)s/\lambda\to2s$ and collapses to $w$. The exterior facet lies at $x=0<t_{\lambda,s}$, so it is always excluded. Finite weighted summation gives the selected rate profile.

On $A_\lambda$ the volume between the two cutoffs is $\int_{t_1}^{t_2}2(x+\lambda)\,dx=\Delta$. Central reflection gives the reverse change of exactly the same volume on $D_\lambda$, with no change on the middle or padding fibers. Thus the symmetric difference is $2\Delta$ and the intersection is $Q-\Delta$. For fixed positive rates, both cutoffs are $O(e^{-\min(s_1,s_2)/\lambda})=o(\lambda)$, which gives the claimed ordinary volume bound. The limiting positive-rate densities differ by the density $2$ on the interval between the two rates, so the total variation norm of their difference is $2|s_1-s_2|$.

statement:
Fix $0<\lambda\le1/4$. Put $A_\lambda=\{(x,y):0\le x\le1,\ |y|\le x+\lambda\}$, $c=(1,0)$, $D_\lambda=2c-A_\lambda$, and $B_\lambda=(A_\lambda+D_\lambda)/2$. At integer bases $z=0,1,2$, use these three fibers with their summed planar area. They are the exact integer fibers of the hull of the lifted endpoints. The center $Y=(1,1,0)$ is globally deepest in this core. Its raw depth is $Q=7/4+3\lambda$, and each $H_t=\{x+(t-1)z\ge t\}$, $0<t<1$, attains $Q$ there and has proper own trace and full physical section centroid $Y$.

There is also an actual padded family in integer dimension two. Put the core at $r=0$ and add the rectangle $[3,4]\times[-1/2,1/2]$ at each of the 25 sites $(z,1)$, $z=0,\ldots,24$, then take the convex hull. These are precisely the 28 integer fibers. The sum of their areas is $M=57/2+6\lambda$, each fiber has area at most $2<M/9$, and the core center at $r=0$ still has raw depth $Q$ and maximizes depth within its own fiber. The caps $H_t=\{x+(t-1)z-100r\ge t\}$ attain $Q$ there with unchanged section centroid. The padded center $(z,r,x,y)=(12,1,7/2,0)$ has depth at least $25/2>Q$, while $Q/M<1/9$ at the core anchor. A finite menu at the core anchor can also include both signs of both continuous coordinate normals, all still attaining $Q$.

On either family, for any fixed $T>0$ use the affine denominator $L_\lambda=C_\lambda(x+\epsilon_\lambda)>0$ with $\int\log L_\lambda\,d\mu_\lambda=0$ and $\min L_\lambda=e^{-T/\lambda}$, where $\mu_\lambda$ is the original mixed measure. Given any finite list of rates $s_i\in(0,T)$, set $t_{\lambda,s_i}=C_\lambda^{-1}e^{-s_i/\lambda}-\epsilon_\lambda\in(0,1)$ for small $\lambda$. For $R_\lambda=-\lambda\log L_\lambda$, the pushforward of $\lVert\nabla_x L_\lambda\rVert\,d\mu_\lambda/L_\lambda$ from $A_\lambda$ under the physical-position and rate map converges on positive rates to $2\delta_w\otimes\operatorname{Leb}|_{(0,T)}$, where $w$ is the point at base zero and $x=y=0$. Its restriction by the actual cap at rate $s$ converges there to $2\delta_w\otimes\operatorname{Leb}|_{(0,s)}$. The weighted log measure $(-\log L_\lambda)_+$ times section length on the proper $A_\lambda$ trace converges to $2s\delta_{(w,s)}$, and each such cap misses the exterior $x=0$ facet. A finite probability menu of weights $p_i$ has selected positive-rate density $2\sum_i p_i\mathbf1_{R<s_i}\delta_w$ for almost every $R>0$.

For $0<t_1<t_2<1$, put $\Delta=t_2^2-t_1^2+2\lambda(t_2-t_1)$. The ordinary symmetric difference of the caps has mass $2\Delta$ and their intersection has mass $Q-\Delta$ on both families. For distinct fixed rates the symmetric difference is $O(\lambda e^{-\min(s_1,s_2)/\lambda})$, while the total variation of the difference of the limiting selected positive-rate inverse measures is $2|s_1-s_2|$.
title: Equal critical volumes allow prescribed finite inverse-rate oscillation
